transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I barely sleep in any useful way anymore. I'll just lie awake at night, replaying client models in my head. And then when I do finally drift off, I just wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning with my stomach completely tight. I end up going to work feeling like I never actually rested at all. It's just really taking a toll on me.
How long has this sleep problem been going on?
It's been going on for about three years now. It started right around the time our company had a big merger and they completely reorganized our Caribbean-market division.
Besides the sleep problems, have you been feeling worried or anxious during the day, even when things seem to be going okay?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel worried or anxious during the day. I mean, I don't sit around stressing about things if everything at work is going okay. It's really just... I'm just incredibly drained from not sleeping.
During these past three years with the sleep problems, have you noticed that things you used to enjoy doing don't seem as interesting or fun to you anymore?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I mean, I still like doing the things I've always liked doing. It's just that I'm so exhausted all the time from not sleeping that I don't always have the energy for them. But the interest is still there, I just... I'm just too tired most of the time.

Have you had any medical workup done for your sleep problems, such as seeing a sleep specialist or having a sleep study? And have you noticed any other physical symptoms or health changes over these three years besides the sleep issues?

No, I haven't seen a sleep specialist or had a sleep study done. I guess I just kept hoping it would get better on its own, or that if work settled down, my sleep would too. And as for other physical symptoms... no, I haven't really noticed anything else. Just the exhaustion from being awake so much at night.
When you wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning, are you able to fall back asleep, or do you find yourself staying awake for the rest of the night?
No, I usually can't get back to sleep. I just... I lie there awake for the rest of the night. Once I'm up at 3 or 4, that's pretty much it for me. I just wait for the alarm to go off.
Over these past three years, have you noticed that your mood has been persistently low or depressed, even on days when things at work are going well?

Yes, I have. Most days I just move through the office, and even my apartment, with this... this heavy, gray feeling. It's like I'm just going through the motions. And honestly, I'm often just trying not to cry when someone asks me a normal question. It doesn't really matter if work is going well or not, that feeling is just kind of always there.

Besides the sleep problems and the heavy feeling you described, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over these three years, or have you had trouble concentrating or making decisions at work?

My appetite and weight have stayed pretty much the same, I think. But my concentration... yes, that's actually been really difficult. 

At work, spreadsheets that used to be second nature to me now take me hours to get through. I just... I lose the thread of what I'm doing. I find myself rereading the exact same financial assumptions over and over again. And even after spending all that extra time on them, I still constantly worry I've missed something completely obvious right before I have to give a presentation. It's just very hard to focus my mind on anything.
Have you had any thoughts about harming yourself or about death during these past three years?

No, I haven't. I mean, I feel miserable most of the time, and I'm exhausted, but I haven't had any thoughts about... about hurting myself or wanting to die. It's just more of a struggle to get through the day, but not that.

You mentioned these feelings have been going on for three years. During that entire time, has the heavy, gray mood and these other problems been pretty constant, or have there been periods of weeks or months where you felt noticeably better?
No, it's been pretty constant. I don't think there's been any time in the last three years where I felt... better, or normal. It's just always there, every day. I haven't had a break from it.

Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energetic, optimistic, or 'high' — where you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt well-rested, or where your thoughts seemed to be racing?

No, I've never had anything like that. I've never felt unusually energetic or... or 'high' like you're describing. And I definitely haven't had times where I needed less sleep and still felt rested. Honestly, it's just been the opposite—just this constant exhaustion and low mood. I've never had a period of racing thoughts or feeling overly optimistic.
